q: List the various types of tensioning device used in prestressed concrete.
What are the different types of flexural failure modes of prestressed concrete beams? Explain with sketches.
Enlist the assumptions of the Strain compatibility method for prestressed concrete.
Distinguish between web shear, flexural and flexure-shear cracks in concrete beam with sketches.
Explain the differences of prestressed concrete over reinforced concrete.
Define transmission length and what is expression of it as per IS 1343 recommendations.
Explain the basic concept of Prestressed Concrete.
Explain IS 1343 recommendations for design of prestressed members subjected to bending and torsion.
What are the advantages and disadvantages of prestressed concrete
Explain the terms: (1) Pretensioning (2) Tendon (3) Anchorage
Explain (1) Bonded Prestressed Concrete (2) Post-tensioning (3) Degree of Prestressing.
Explain the concept of thrust line in PSC sections
Explain difference between time dependent and immediate losses in prestressed concrete sections.
Enlist the advantages of composite construction with prestressed and in situ concrete for structural members.

A Pretensioned prestressed concrete beam of rectangular section 150 mm wide and 350 mm deep has effective cover of 50 mm. If fck = 40MPa, fp = 1600 MPa and Ap = 461 mm2, Calculate ultimate flexural strength using IS code provisions.
Define the losses present in post-tensioned member.
State the assumptions made in the design of prestressed concrete members for the limit state of collapse in flexure.
Explain drying shrinkage strain and autogenous shrinkage strain.
Explain the terms: end block, anchorage zone.
Enlist various loads acting on bridges.

A bonded prestressed concrete beam is of rectangular section of width 400 mm and overall depth 1200 mm. The tendons consisting of 3300 mm2 of standard strands with characteristic strength of 1700 N/mm2. The strands are located at 870 mm from the top face of the beam. The characteristic cube strength of concrete is 60 N/mm2. Estimate the ultimate moment capacity of section using IS 1343 (2012) recommendations.

A prestressed rectangular concrete bam 200 mm wide and 600 mm deep is supporting a live load of 8kN/m over a span of 8 m. Find the effective prestressing force in the parabolic cable having an eccentricity of 80 mm at the center of span and concentric at the supports. Case 1) In this beam the bending effect of the prestressing force is nullified by the imposed load for the mid span section, neglecting self weight of the beam. Case 2) if the resultant force due to self weight, LL and prestressing force is zero at the soffit of the beam at the center of span section.
Explain stress distribution in the end block in the prestressed concrete beam.
Under what situations and types of structures would you recommended the use of unbounded tendons?
Enlist the formula for calculation of Moment of resistance of Flanged sections as per IS 1343 recommendations.
What is the need for the use of high strength concrete and tensile steel in prestressed concrete?
State the four fundamental conditions for stresses at transfer and service stage.
Justify why high-strength concrete and high-tensile steel are essential in prestressed concrete.
Define the term Pressure Line or Thrust Line in a prestressed concrete beam. How is it related to the Load Balancing Concept?

A prestressed concrete beam 300 mm x 500 mm is post tensioned by a parabolic cable with an eccentricity of 50 mm at the center and concentric at the supports, prestressing force is 500 kN. Estimate loss of prestress in cable due to creep of concrete. Take modular ratio 6 and creep coefficient as 3.0.

A rectangular beam of size 300×600 mm is prestressed by 8 wires of 9 mm diameter with their centroid at 50 mm below the centroidal axis of the beam. Initial prestress = 2000 N/mm2, fck= 50 N/mm2, Es=210 kN/mm2, relaxation loss = 5%, creep coefficient= 1.6, Total shrinkage strain = 3×10−4, Age of loading = 28 days, Relative humidity 60%, Calculate: (i) Loss of prestress due to elastic shortening of concrete (ii) Loss due to creep of concrete (iii) Loss due to shrinkage of concrete (iv) Loss due to relaxation of stress in steel
List the factors influencing the short term and long-term deflections of prestressed concrete members.

A pre-tensioned T-section has a flange 1200 mm wide and 200 mm thick. The rib is 250 mm wide and 450 mm deep. The effective depth of cross section is 600 mm. The high tensile steel has an area of 800 mm2. If the characteristic cube strength of concrete and tensile strength of steel is 50 and 1860 N/mm2 respectively, calculate the flexural strength of the T-section.

A rectangular concrete beam having section 150 × 450 mm is prestressed by a parabolic cable carrying initial prestressing force of 400 kN. The cable has an eccentricity of 100 mm at the center of span and is concentric at the supports. If span of the beam is 10 m and live load 4 kN/m, estimate short term deflection. Assuming E=35 kN/mm2 and creep coefficient is 2.0, loss of prestress = 15% of initial prestress after 6 months, estimate long term deflection at the center of the span, assuming that dead load and live loads are simultaneously acting after the release of prestress.
Explain the modes of failure in prestressed concrete beams subjected to combined bending, shear and torsion.

The support section of a prestressed concrete beam, 200 mm wide by 400 mm deep is required to support an ultimate shear force of 180 kN. The compressive prestress at the centroid axis is 6 N/mm2. The characteristic cube strength of concrete is 50 N/mm2, the cover to reinforcement is 40 mm. If the characteristic tensile strength of stirrups is 500 N/mm2, design suitable shear reinforcement in the section as per the IS: 1343-2012.
Explain elastic design of prestressed tension members.

A prestressed concrete beam span 12 m of rectangular section 200 mm wide and 450 mm deep is axially prestressed by a cable carrying an effective force of 350 kN. The beam supports total udl of 7 kN/m including self-weight. Compare the magnitude of principal tensile stress in the beam with and without axial prestress.
List various types of prestressed tension and compression members.

A pre-tensioned concrete beam, 100 mm wide and 300 mm deep, is prestressed by straight wires carrying an initial force of 150 kN at an eccentricity of 50 mm the Modulus of Elasticity of steel and concrete are 210 and 35 kN/m2 respectively. Estimate the percentage loss of stress in steel due to elastic deformation of concrete if the area of steel wires is 188 mm2.
Discuss the maximum allowable compressive stress limits in flexure due to prestressing at both the service stage and transfer stage for post- tensioned and pre-tensioned members, as per IS:1343-2012.
Enlist the formula for calculating losses due to Elastic deformation and Friction in prestressed concrete sections
Explain with sketch IS 1343 recommendations for computing the Moment of resistance of rectangular section.
Enlist different types of flexural failure and explain any one in detail.

A concrete beam is prestressed by a cable with initial prestressing force of 300 kN. The cross sectional area of wires in the cable is 300 mm2. Calculate the percentage loss of stress in the cable only due to shrinkage, if the beam is Pretensioned. Assume Es = 210 kN/mm2.
Differentiate between Pre-tensioning and Post-tensioning.
Elaborate anchorage slip. How do you compute the loss of stress due to anchorage slip?

A rectangular concrete beam, 360 mm deep and 200 mm wide, is prestressed by means of fifteen 5 mm diameter wires located 65 mm from the bottom of the beam and three 5 mm wires, located 25 mm from the top of the beam. If the wires are initially tensioned to a stress of 840 N/mm², calculate the percentage loss of stress in steel immediately after transfer, allowing for the loss of stress due to elastic deformation of concrete only. Es = 210 kN/mm² & Ec=31.5 kN/mm²
List the various types of loss of prestress in pre-tensioned and post- tensioned members.
Briefly explain Strain Compatibility method.
Distinguish between creep and shrinkage.

The cross-section of a symmetrical I-section prestressed beam is 300 mm by 700 mm (overall), with flange and web 100 mm thick. The beam is posttensioned by cables containing 40 wires of 5 mm diameter high-tensile steel wires at an eccentricity of 200mm. The 28- days strength of concrete incompression is 40N/mm2. Assuming that the grouting of the tendons is 100 percent effective, determine the ultimate moment of resistance of the section using IS 1343 (2012) recommendations.
Distinguish between Pre-tensioned and Post-tensioned Concrete members.

An unsymmetrical I section having top flange 750 x 200 mm bottom flange 450 x 250 mm thickness of web 150mm overall depth 1000mm.If permissible tensile and compressive stress at transfer and working load are not to exceed zero in tension 15 N/mm2 in compression.Determine P and e to resist self weight and applied moment 1012 kNm and 450 kNm. Assume loss of pre stress 15%.
What is creep in prestressed concrete? What are the factors that affect creep of concrete?

A PSC beam of 230 mm wide and 450 mm deep is used over an span of 4m is pre stressed by a cable carrying a force of 650 kN & located at an eccentricity of 75 mm. The beam supports three concentrated loads of 25 kN at each quarter span points. Determine the location of the pressure line in beam at centre, quarter & support sections. Neglect the moment due to self weight of the beam
Explain transmission length in pre-tensioned members.

A PSC beam of span 8m has the following data: Area =32×103 mm2 E=38 kN/m2, width of gyration 72 mm Cable: parabolic, 6 wires of 7 mm HTS, concentric at supports and eccentric by 50mm at mid span. Fpe= 1000 N/mm2 Determine the deflection for the following cases: i) Self weight+ Prestress ii) ii) Self weight + Prestress +Live load of 3 kN/m

A beam of symmetrical I-section spanning 8 m has flange width of 150 mm and flange thickness of 80 mm respectively. The overall depth of the beam is 450 mm. Thickness of web is 80 mm. The beam is prestressed by a parabolic cable with an eccentricity of 150 mm at the centre of the span and zero at the supports. The Live Load on the beam is 3kN/m. (1) Determine the effective force in the cable for balancing the Dead Load and Live Load on the beams (2) Calculate the shift of the pressure line from the tendon centre line.
Explain the concept of load balancing.
